newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most shares flat on Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: Most shares flat on Beirut bourse.

text.p: Most shares were flat on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday but brokers said a U.S. decision to lift its travel ban on Lebanon might boost Solidere shares.
Bank of Beirut shares hit a record high of $5.5 from $5.25. Brokers expect the share to reach $6 next week.
There was no trade in Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce for the first time since its debut on the bourse last December. The shares traded at $22.25 on Tuesday.

"I think that bank shares have reached a ceiling. Objectively speaking, one should say at least that banks are fairly valued," Jean Riache, chairman of Beirut finance house Financial Funds Advisors, said.
"BOB is still moving. This means there is still room left in this sector," he added.
BSE turnover climbed to 298,430 shares from 233,746 for a value of $3,490,593 against $2,630,369.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.56 percent to 195.99. The BLOM general index fell 0.70 percent to 1106.58 and the LISPI climbed 0.25 percent to 96.74.
Solidere A fell to $12.875 from $13 while B held steady at $13.00.
The United States on Wednesday lifted the 12-year-old travel ban on U.S. citizens visiting Lebanon after receiving pledges from the government in Beirut to do more to fight terrorism.
Asked whether the move would affect market activity, Riache said: "Let's wait and see tomorrow".
The market had already closed before the U.S. decision was announced.
"We might have a positive impact on Solidere shares because the company is tied to the macroeconomic picture in the country. I think Solidere is sensitive to this kind of news," he added.
A bloc of 96,802 Solidere A shares traded on the floor at $13.
Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, is leading a multi-billion dollar reconstruction drive in Beirut.
Banque Audi was unchanged at $27.8750 and Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.2813.
There was no trade in the other listed industrial firms -- Uniceramic, Ciments Blanc and Eternit .
